How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

I changed nothing. All the figure and permission rules are listed below, named as the code names them. Paths are relative to `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` (Java) and `src/main/frontend/features/` (TS).

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Which claims count
- **Status** (`ClaimStatus.counts()` / `isOpen()`): only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count. DRAFT and VOID never do. PENDING is treated as open: it goes overdue, takes the late charge and can be held.
- **Live totals** (`Person.counts(claim)`, mirrored in TS by `live()` + `heldOn()`): a counting claim is left out when any of these is true:
  - it is deferred (`isDeferred`: OPEN and the sheet's today is before `deferredUntil`);
  - it is OPEN or PENDING and its **date** falls in one of the person's holds (`Hold.covers`, both ends inclusive, `to` may be open);
  - it is OPEN or PENDING and the sheet's today has reached the person's retirement date (`retiredOut`).
  
  The hold and retirement exclusions don't apply when a statement binds the claim, but a PENDING claim never counts as bound.
- **Correction** (`isCorrection`): a negative amount. It must name a SETTLED claim of the same person (`corrects`), and it gets no floor and no late charge.

### A claim's figures
- **due** (`Figures.due`, TS `claimDueCents`). Worked out in this order:
  1. If it has a frozen `due` (set when settled), show that.
  2. Otherwise take its **figure** (`Figures.figure`): the `statedDue` its person's last statement bound it to (ignored while PENDING), or failing that the **live** value.
  3. **live** (`Figures.live`, TS `dueCents`) = amount × the rate in force on the claim's date for the person's grade on that date (`Rates.pct` / `rateOn`; a rate has a from-date and an optional to-date) ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals. With no rate it is null and shows "n/a".
  4. Add the **late charge**.
  5. Raise the result to at least the **floor** in force on the claim's date (`Settings.floor`, default 1.00).
- **Rounding** (`Figures.rounding`, sent to the screen as `halfUp`): HALF_UP when the claim is dated before the sheet's **policy date**, otherwise HALF_EVEN. When no policy date is set, the sheet's today is used. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
- **due-by** (`DueBy.of` / `BuildClaim`): fixed when the claim is added. It is the Nth business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays. N (the terms) is the person's own `terms`, else the grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's terms (default 14).
  - The terms used are stored as `dueTerms`.
  - Later changes to the terms, re-dating the claim, or editing its date do not move the due-by.
  - Adding a holiday on or before the due-by recomputes it with the same terms, unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID (`RefixDueBys`).
- **overdue** (`Figures.overdue`): the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and due-by + grace is before the sheet's today. Grace is `grace-<grade>`, read as in force on the claim's date (default 0).
- **Late charge** (`Figures.charge`, TS `lateChargeCents`):
  - It is counted per full 30 days past due-by + grace.
  - At each 30-day boundary, it adds `late-pct` (as in force on that boundary date) of (figure + the charges so far), so it compounds.
  - Each step is rounded with the claim's rounding mode.
  - It always follows the sheet's today and is never frozen by a statement.
- **number** (`ClaimNumbers`): given when the claim is opened. It is sheet-wide (`7`), or, while `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, numbered within the period containing the due-by (`P1-2`), or `X-n` when no period contains it. A voided claim keeps its number, and numbers are never reused.
- **period** (`claim-period`): the period that contains the claim's **due-by**, not its date.
- **Other claim fields**: `lateEntry` (the claim was added while a soft-closed period contained its due-by), `deferred`/`deferredUntil`, `proofs`, `splitFrom`, `remindedOn` (once per sheet-today), `batch` (from bulk settle), `stated`/`statedDue`, `log`.

### A person's figures (TS `claims.slot.tsx` → `PersonClaims`; Java `Rollup.snapshot`)
- **claimed**: the sum of amounts of the claims that count in the live totals.
- **due-total**: the sum of those claims' dues, then capped at the **cap** in force on the sheet's today.
  - It is n/a when there is no rate today for the person's current grade *and* no claim has a figure.
  - An n/a total is not capped.
- **excess**: how far the due-total is over the cap.
- **settled-total / open-total**: the uncapped due-total split into SETTLED claims and OPEN+PENDING claims. These exist only in the front end.
- **overdue-count / overdue-total**: the count and the summed dues of overdue claims (the total skips n/a).
- **aged 0–30 / 31–60 / 61+** (`aging.slot`): dues of counting open claims, grouped by days from the claim's date to today. Not capped.
- **backing** (`patrons.slot`): the frozen dues of the patrons' SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days.
- **active** (`active.ts`): the person has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days.
- **grade**: the grade in force on the sheet's today. Grades are dated; the first one applies from the beginning of time.
- **Statement figures**: `statementCount`, `statedTotal` and `statementDate`.
- **Per-period due-total** (`personPeriodDueCents`, `PeriodCloser`):
  - The claims whose due-by is in the period and that counted by their **status at the period's end** (read from the status log).
  - Once the period is closed, the figure fixed at closing is shown instead (0.00 for a person added since).

### Sheet figures
- **rollup / header totals** (`useSheetTotals`, `Rollup`):
  - The claimed-total is a plain sum.
  - The due-total and overdue-total leave out the single highest and lowest person when three or more people have a figure (`trimmedTotal`).
  - n/a people are skipped.
- **summary**: per-grade figures cover non-retired people only. There are also counts per status and per void reason.
- **month and tag totals**: uncapped sums of counting claims' dues. A claim with two tags counts in both.
- **header people count**: includes retired people.

### What freezes and when
- **Settle and approve** freeze `due` at the figure as it stands then (bound or live, plus the late charge, at least the floor). With no rate the due stays live.
- **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes `due` again at today's unbound live figure.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`):
  - Binds each counting claim to its figure *without* the charge or floor; every other claim is unbound.
  - Records the capped due-total.
  - It can be taken as of a past date (`AsOf` rebuilds the sheet from trigger history).
  - Bindings are removed by a split, a reassignment, or cancelling the statement (`CancelStatement`, steward only). Cancelling does not restore earlier bindings.
- **Period close** fixes the period's total and each person's total. A soft close fixes the figures but still allows changes; a hard close refuses every change to claims whose due-by falls in the period (`ClosedPeriods.refuse`).
  - Auto-close: when today changes and the sheet has grace days, every open period whose to-date + grace days is before the new today is closed.
  - Reopening makes the totals live again.
- **Changing today** releases all edit locks and writes SNAPSHOT audit lines.

### Who may do what
- **Roles** (`Settings.role`): CLERK by default, STEWARD, or VIEWER. A delegation that covers today makes the user a STEWARD.
- **Permission matrix** (`Settings.allows`):
  - open, settle, void and close: clerk and steward by default.
  - reassign and reopen: steward by default.
  - A viewer may do none of these, and nobody may on an archived sheet. `ViewerGuard` also rejects every POST/PUT from a viewer, and from anyone on an archived sheet, except the bulk actions.
- **Settle, approve and void** (`ApplyClaimStatus`):
  - The user who opened a claim, or last edited it, may not settle or approve it.
  - A clerk settling a claim whose due is over the **clerk limit** sends it to PENDING; the limit is the one in force on today, not the claim's date.
  - Only a steward approves a PENDING claim. Rejecting it sends it back to OPEN.
  - A claim whose due is over the proof threshold (grade's, else sheet's) needs proofs before it can be settled or approved.
  - A claim whose due is over the note threshold can't be opened without a note.
  - A deferred claim can't be settled.
  - A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, within 7 days (`SETTLED_VOID_DAYS`).
  - When the sheet has void reasons, a void needs one of them.
- **Steward-only actions**: re-date, re-settle, cancel statement, archive.
- **Edit locks**: only a DRAFT can be edited, and another user's open editor locks the claim.
- **Retirement**: a claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused.

### Import, paste and bulk actions
- **Paste** (`ValidatePasteClaims` / `AddPastedClaims`):
  - Each line is `name,amount,date,note`, and a trailing ` #ref` sets the reference.
  - All or nothing: every line is built with the claim form's rules first, so one bad line refuses the whole paste.
  - References must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case.
- **Quick-add**: creates the person as grade A if the name is new, then adds the claim dated the entry date (else today).
- **Bulk actions**:
  - Bulk settle is all or nothing, with one batch number.
  - Bulk open and bulk reassign go item by item and count the refusals.
  - Bulk grade works like saving the person form for each selected person.

## 2. How hard this was to follow

It's scattered and duplicated. The core money rules sit in a few readable places, mainly `Figures.java`, `Person.counts`, `Settings` and `ApplyClaimStatus`, and their Javadoc is unusually complete. But every figure rule is written twice: once in Java (used for audit, statements, settling and period closing) and once in TypeScript (`useClaims.ts`, `useRates.ts`, `usePeriods.ts`, which is what the screen shows). The rest is spread across about 110 one-method OfficeFloor step classes, a servlet filter, a DB-trigger history mechanism and about ten front-end slots. A new developer would have to read both copies side by side to be sure they agree.
